t: LeetCode 2164 — Sort Even and Odd Indices Independently
o: We rearrange nums so that values sitting at even indices read in ascending order left-to-right, while values at odd indices read in descending order — the two parity classes are sorted independently and written back into place. Starting from [4,1,2,3], the odd-indexed values 1,3 become 3,1 and the even-indexed 4,2 become 2,4, giving [2,3,4,1]. Example 2 reminds us a length-2 array changes nothing, since each class holds a single element. Constraints are tiny — n and every nums[i] are at most 100 — so extraction plus comparison sort passes easily, and the bounded value range even permits a counting-sort refinement.
k: Even- and odd-indexed values never interact: partition by index parity, sort each part in its requested direction, then weave back.
Values are capped at 100, so counting sort achieves O(n + 100) instead of O(n log n).
For odd positions 'non-increasing' simply means iterating the value range from 100 downwards.

a.i: Collect the values at even indices and sort them ascending; collect the values at odd indices and sort them descending. Writing the two sorted streams back to their original parity positions yields the answer directly. This is the most natural reading of the two rules and is optimal up to the log factor.
s: Extract nums[0], nums[2], ... into one list and nums[1], nums[3], ... into another.
Sort the even-index list non-decreasingly and the odd-index list non-increasingly.
Write the sorted lists back into their respective parity positions.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def sortEvenOdd(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        evens = sorted(nums[::2])
        odds = sorted(nums[1::2], reverse=True)
        nums[::2] = evens
        nums[1::2] = odds
        return nums

a.t: O(n log n) — two comparison sorts over ~n/2 elements each

a.n: Approach 2: Counting sort over the value range (linear)
a.i: Since every value lies in 1..100, keep separate occurrence counts for even-indexed and odd-indexed positions. Rebuild the answer left to right: even positions emit ascending values from bucket 0 while odd positions emit descending values from bucket 1, advancing/decrementing a pointer per class. This trades the log factor for a fixed 101-wide sweep.
s: Count occurrences of each value 1..100 separately for even and odd index classes.
Maintain scan pointers e ascending from 0 and o descending from 100.
For each position i, emit the current pointer value of its class, decrement that count, and advance the pointer when exhausted.
a.t: O(n + V) with V = 101 distinct values — counting plus one weave pass
a.sp: O(V) — two count arrays of size 101

w: A warm-up problem — use it to show clean partition-sort-weave code, then volunteer the counting-sort upgrade for O(n + V). Pitfalls: reversing the wrong class (odd must be NON-INCREASING), off-by-one when weaving (position i takes index i//2 of its class list), and forgetting arrays may have odd length so the even class is one larger. Follow-ups: three-way index mod 3 classes with different orders, stability requirements, or streaming input.
